mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Applicable commercial registry or chamber of commerce in the parent company's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin state is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of Board Resolutions approving the incorporation of the Spanish SL and appointing the attorney-in-fact
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the non-resident corporate shareholder; notarized in the jurisdiction of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, followed by official sworn translation into Spanish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized UBO declaration (declaración de titularidad real) identifying all natural persons holding more than 25% ownership or control

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of the managing director and all UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent notary, civil registry, or consular officer in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; sworn translation into Spanish if the document is not already in Spanish

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory due diligence screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorised signatories against: (i) the EU Financial Sanctions Database implementing UN Security Council resolutions; (ii) the Spanish official gazette and Council of Ministers sanctioned-persons lists; (iii) PEP categories defined in Article 14.2 of Ley 10/2010, extended to second-degree relatives and close associates; and (iv) the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons list as a voluntary best-practice control to ensure readiness for USD-denominated wire transactions. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least ten years after the termination of the business relationship pursuant to Article 42 of Ley 10/2010. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) is triggered automatically when any UBO is a PEP, a resident of a high-risk third country, or when the transaction contains unusual or opaque ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online service for the 'certificación negativa de denominación social' at www.rmc.es
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A Spanish SL may adopt a denomination expressed in any language, but the name must be written in the Latin alphabet without foreign diacritical marks; where a foreign-language word is used, the articles of association must include a Spanish transcription or transliteration. The name must not be contrary to law, morality, or public order, and must not mislead as to the corporate form. For an industrial edge-computing business, a name such as 'Industrial Edge Computing, S.L.' or 'Informática Industrial Perimetral, S.L.' is acceptable and should include the statutory abbreviation 'S.L.' in all correspondence.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Casa Real, Rey, Reina, Princesa, Corona
España, Gobierno, Estado, Administración, Ministerio, Delegación del Gobierno
Banco de España, Instituto Nacional, Consejo de Ministros, Tribunal Supremo, Consejo General del Poder Judicial
Colegio Oficial, Cámara Oficial, Federación, Confederación, Mutualidad when not duly authorised
Registro Mercantil, Registro de la Propiedad, Notaría, Agencia Tributaria
Abogado, Procurador, Notario, Registrador, Auditoría, Inspección when not supported by the required professional qualification or prior ministerial approval
S.A., S.L., S.C., S.Com. and similar corporate abbreviations not corresponding to the chosen corporate type
International, Mundial, Europeo, Nacional when used in a way that suggests governmental or supranational authority without prior administrative authorisation
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon a definitive refusal by the Registro Mercantil Central, the applicant may, within one month from notification, file an administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública of the Ministry of Justice. The appeal must attach the original refusal notice, the proposed denomination, and a legal-basis brief demonstrating that the proposed name does not create confusion with existing Spanish registrations, does not encroach on reserved official or professional terms, and satisfies the language and transliteration rules. Alternatively, the applicant may immediately submit a new application for one or more alternative names; parallel reservations of alternatives are permitted. Judicial review before the Spanish national courts becomes available only after the administrative appeal is exhausted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole registered-office solution for an industrial edge-computing manufacturer. The Spanish Commercial Registry and the Tax Agency (AEAT) will accept a formal 'domicilio social' at a business centre or shared-office suite only where a genuine physical postal address is maintained and there is at least one employee or authorised representative able to receive notifications on the premises. Given the industrial nature of the business and the need for installation, testing, warehousing, and after-sales support, a pure virtual office (no physical access, no staff, no operational substance) would be rebutted for corporate tax residency and Spanish commercial-registry purposes. A physical office or light-assembly/warehouse facility is therefore mandatory to satisfy commercial-substance requirements under Ley de Sociedades de Capital and AEAT's interpretation of place-of-effective-management rules.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 67% estimated probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by AEAT or the Commercial Registry during the first 36 months after incorporation, driven by the cross-border nature of the operations, the use of a registered office at a multi-tenant suite, and the necessity to open a Spanish VAT and customs registration. If the chosen registered office is a virtual office, the estimated probability increases to above 85%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-10 and related provisions of the Código de Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital requirement of 3,000 EUR for SL, fully subscribed and paid up in cash at incorporation; no escrow account mandated beyond standard banking verification
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The Board of Directors of the proposed Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada resolves as follows: (1) to approve incorporation with share capital of three thousand euros (EUR 3,000), fully subscribed and paid up by the incorporators in equal proportions; (2) to adopt the registered office at [pro forma address, e.g. Calle Ejemplo 123, 28001 Madrid, Spain]; (3) to appoint [name] as sole Administrator and [name] as Secretary; (4) to authorize the Managing Director to execute all documents, file the incorporation deed with the Registro Mercantil Central, and commence operations. This resolution ensures compliance with statutory minimum capital, governance, and formalities under the LSRL, enabling immediate formation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation of Articles of Association and Share Subscription
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a Spanish notary to draft the public deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) specifying company name, share capital, registered office, and subscriber details. Incorporators must present valid identification and sign the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary queries the application, provide additional documentation or amend the articles and resubmit for authentication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the signed deed to the notary for authentication, pay applicable fees, and obtain certified copies of the deed.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Request clarification from the notary and revise the deed if necessary before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Registration with Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central or Provincial Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized deed together with a registration request form, pay registry fees, and obtain the certificate of incorporation and registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of no impediment if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, supply missing documents or file an appeal within the statutory period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Tax Identification Number and Mandatory Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) and Social Security Administration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online or in person for the NIF (tax identification number), register the company for social security contributions, and complete any required fiscal and labor filings.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit supplementary evidence if requested by the tax or social security authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Industria, Comercio y Turismo or competent regional government authority

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico or regional environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Directive 2010/75/EU on industrial emissions, wastewater discharge limits per Royal Decree 1/2016, and VOC emission thresholds

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from local fire brigade, structural load verification by qualified engineer, and workplace safety clearance from labor authorities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT); electronic portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Spanish S.L. obtains a provisional NIF via Form 036/037 at incorporation, followed by a definitive NIF after registration in the Registro Mercantil. A non-resident foreign entity without a permanent establishment obtains an NIF for non-resident taxpayers through Form 036, generally appointing a tax representative when required; applications are filed electronically with supporting documents, including power of attorney, incorporation excerpt, and identification of the legal representative.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not apply US-style check-the-box elections; residency and classification are determined by Spanish law. Elective regimes include the Spanish corporate tax consolidation group election under Ley 27/2014, art. 67 et seq., the ETVE non-resident holding regime, and the tax-neutral merger/split regime. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD are applied automatically and do not require a taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido — IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 0 for established Spanish entities; VAT registration is compulsory upon commencement of taxable activities with no general economic threshold. Intra-Community distance sales to Spanish consumers are registrable above EUR 10,000 unless the EU One-Stop-Shop regime is used; non-established foreign suppliers may rely on the reverse charge for B2B supplies and must register for distance sales if the threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Large enterprises (annual turnover exceeding EUR 6 million) must submit VAT book-level data to AEAT through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) within four days, using certified XML/API interfaces. Law 18/2022 (Crea y Crece) requires all entrepreneurs and professionals to issue electronic invoices in B2B transactions and maintain interoperable formats such as Facturae. Royal Decree 1007/2023 (Verifactu) requires certified billing systems to generate a QR code and SHA-256 hash, and to keep tamper-proof records accessible to the tax authorities.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to third territories outside the EU are zero-rated under Ley 37/1992, art. 21, provided the goods are physically transported out of the EU and the exporter holds the accepted customs export declaration. The exemption also covers qualifying transport and ancillary services directly connected to exported goods. Offshore services supplied to non-resident business customers may be outside the scope of Spanish VAT under art. 69, subject to B2B reverse charge and substantiation of the recipient's business status.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Documento Único Administrativo — DUA) accepted by Spanish Customs
Transport evidence of EU exit: Bill of Lading, CMR, AWB, or equivalent multimodal document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank confirmation of funds received for the export transaction
Certified proof of departure (e.g., DEXIE / EXS Exit Summary Declaration) where issued
Origin documentation (EUR-1, ATR, or invoice declaration) when preferential origin is claimed
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT may verify export documentation within the general limitation period of four years, or longer for unclear or material omissions. Unsupported zero-rating claims are retrospectively reversed, with assessed VAT and late-payment interest. Penalties under Ley General Tributaria, arts. 191–194 range from 50% to 150% of the underpaid tax depending on negligence, concealment, or fraudulent conduct. Intentional falsification of export evidence may escalate to criminal tax fraud prosecution under art. 305 of the Penal Code when the defrauded amount exceeds EUR 120,000, carrying fines and imprisonment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) acting as the national competent authority for banking supervision, balance-of-payments statistical reporting, and foreign investment registration, within the framework of the European System of Central Banks and the Single Supervisory Mechanism
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a member of the Eurozone, operates a fully liberalized currency regime. Both current account transactions (including trade in goods and services, royalties, dividends, and interest) and capital account transactions (direct investment, portfolio investment, loans, and financial guarantees) are convertible without exchange control authorization. Profit remittance is permitted without foreign-exchange constraints; however, outbound dividend payments to non-resident shareholders may be subject to withholding tax under domestic law and applicable tax treaties. The practical hurdles are not exchange-related but administrative and documentary: banks require correct declaration of the transaction, identification of the ultimate beneficial owner, and justification of the underlying business activity. Balanced-payments forms must be filed through the Banco de España resident declaration system for transactions with non-residents exceeding EUR 50,000 (RDL 1816/1991 and Banco de España Circular 1/2012).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no mandatory surrender requirements or statutory conversion ratios for export proceeds in Spain. Exporters are free to retain receipts in EUR or in any convertible currency in their accounts with Spanish banks or abroad. No timeline is prescribed for repatriation; however, export proceeds must be reported for balance-of-payments statistical purposes via the declaración de operaciones exteriores when the transaction exceeds the EUR 50,000 threshold. Invoices and transport documents must be preserved for AML, customs, and VAT audit purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for EU/EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions operating under the single passport regime and registered with the Banco de España for passported services; Low for offshore, non-EU/EEA EMIs. Legal constraints: offshore digital EMIs without an EU/EEA banking or e-money licence cannot obtain payment account numbers in Spain, are not connected to TARGET2 or the Spanish local clearing infrastructure, and are generally prohibited from soliciting deposits or providing payment accounts that look like domestic Spanish IBANs. EU-licensed EMIs may provide cross-border payment services, issue e-money, and manage operational accounts, but they cannot grant credit or hold client funds in unsupervised pools. Onboarding requires demonstrated compliance with the Spanish anti-money-laundering law (Ley 10/2010), SEPBLAC registration, and adequate sanctions screening.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: In practice, the managing director or the appointed legal representative with power of attorney (apoderado mancomunado/ solidario) must attend a physical KYC interview at the Spanish bank branch for the initial onboarding of a non-resident corporate entity. Remote opening is available at certain banks only for low-risk profiles and when the representative holds a recognized electronic signature (DNI electrónico or qualified certificate) or when video-identification software is used with notarized corporate documents and apostilles. For shareholders or directors residing in high-risk jurisdictions, physical appearance and sworn translations of corporate documents are compulsory. Powers of attorney granted abroad must be notarized, apostilled, and filed with the notary and the Commercial Registry if they are to be used for banking formalities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque corporate chain with non-resident beneficial owners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current certified register extract (certificación del Registro Mercantil) of the Spanish SL; full organizational chart disclosing all natural-person beneficial owners holding more than 25% of shares or control; certified copies of certificate of incorporation, memorandum and articles of association, and register of beneficial owners of each intermediate holding entity; passport or identity card copies of ultimate beneficial owners; proof of residence and tax identification numbers; statutory declarations of source of funds and business purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital deposit and source of wealth not sufficiently documented
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory declaration of capital contribution signed by the shareholders; notarial deed of incorporation specifying bank details and contribution method; bank reference letters from the originating banks; audited financial statements or management accounts of the foreign parent; commercial invoices or purchase agreements supporting future trade flows; clean personal/professional CVs of shareholders and directors demonstrating legitimate asset accumulation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) or residence in a high-risk or sanctioned jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration forms from all directors and shareholders; independent sanctions screening report covering EU, OFAC, UN, and UK lists; evidence of lawful origin of funds from salary, dividends, or asset sales; explanation of the commercial rationale for the Spanish subsidiary as an industrial edge-computing exporter; legal opinion from a Spanish lawyer confirming no breach of EU restrictive measures; ongoing monitoring acceptance letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or disproportional export payment flows to Latin American counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed export contracts with detailed specifications of rugged industrial computers and edge gateways; pro forma invoices and final invoices matching shipment values; transport and customs documentation (e.g., Bill of Lading, commercial invoices, packing lists); proof of underlying hardware purchase and manufacturing costs; bank statements showing consistent business cycles; export declaration records submitted to Spanish Customs; balance-of-payments filing confirmations for transactions above the reporting threshold.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder funds for the incorporation and subsequent equity financing of the Spanish SL must be routed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfer from the foreign corporate account to the SL's dedicated euro account in Spain. The payment reference must state the purpose: 'Aportación de capital a la constitución de la sociedad' or 'Aportación al fondo de maniobra' as appropriate. The Spanish entity must provide to the receiving bank the notarial deed of incorporation, the bank account confirmation letter, and the Foreign Investment Certificate (certificado de inversión exterior) or the corresponding declaration to the Banco de España if the transaction triggers the statistical threshold. The bank will apply ordinary correspondent banking checks and request confirmation of the ultimate origin of funds before crediting. Once credited, the amount must be recorded in the company's books as subscribed and paid-in capital or equity contribution, and the bank certificate of deposit must be retained as evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 (single telegraphic transfers) for low-to-mid value commercial payments and documentary letters of credit (Commercial LC, usually irrevocable and confirmed) for high-value, structured export transactions to Latin American buyers. The Spanish exporter will receive LC proceeds through a confirming bank in Spain or through the advising bank, with settlement in EUR or USD. For recurring trade settlements, a fully automated SWIFT channel or a centralised payment factory using SPEI in Mexico, PIX in Brazil, or local clearing systems is permissible only through the Spanish bank's correspondent network. All outgoing trade disbursements for supplier payments and dealer commissions must be covered by an underlying commercial contract, invoice package, and customs export declaration. Any outbound payment above EUR 50,000 must be reported to the Banco de España within the relevant statistical declaration period.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla FX forwards (forward contract to buy/sell EUR against USD, MXN, CNY, or other freely convertible currencies) executed with a Spanish bank or an EU-authorized credit institution with a master ISDA or local FX master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for currencies subject to local deliverability restrictions, where settlement is made in EUR or USD referencing an official or approved exchange rate
Cross-currency swaps (FX swaps) to manage linked receivable/payable liquidity exposure in EUR, USD, and MXN
FX options (European-style call/put options) for hedging foreign-currency receivables from emerging-market buyers without mandatory execution risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts by the General Meeting of Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 3,000 EUR and potential administrative dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after approval of the annual accounts by the General Meeting of Shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to 3,000 EUR and potential administrative dissolution proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 January of the following fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of 100 EUR per day of delay, maximum 1,500 EUR

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if total assets exceed 2,000,000 EUR, net turnover exceeds 4,000,000 EUR or average number of employees exceeds 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish GAAP (Plan General Contable) or IFRS as adopted in Spain

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual submission of Ultimate Beneficial Owner details to the Registro Mercantil within the annual accounts filing deadline

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% general corporate income tax rate. Newly incorporated entities may generally apply a 15% rate in the first profitable tax period and the immediately following period, subject to statutory conditions and exclusions.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualifying small entities may benefit from reduced rates or accelerated depreciation under applicable legislation. Research, development and technological innovation tax credits, investment incentives, employment-related incentives and deductions for qualifying investments may reduce the effective rate. The 15% newly incorporated entity rate does not generally apply to entities forming part of a group or carrying on a pre-existing business transferred from another entity. Dividend and capital-gain participation exemptions may apply where statutory ownership, holding-period and subsidiary taxation conditions are satisfied.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, Impuesto sobre Sociedades e Impuesto sobre la Renta de no Residentes, régimen de tributación en España de establecimientos permanentes and tax-return annexes, filed electronically through the Spanish Tax Agency AEAT electronic office using an electronic certificate, Cl@ve where permitted, or an authorized representative.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer ending on 31 December, the normal filing period is 1 to 25 July of the following year. If the final day is not a business day, the deadline is extended under the applicable electronic-filing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, tax identification number, registered office, tax period, activity classification, filing type, balance-sheet currency and electronic-contact information.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Spanish SL is resident if incorporated under Spanish law or has its registered office or effective management in Spain. Non-resident shareholders are reported through ownership and related-party information, but the SL files as a Spanish resident entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Accounting profit or loss and tax-base reconciliation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting result before tax adjusted for permanent differences, temporary differences, non-deductible expenses, exempt income, impairment adjustments, depreciation differences, provisions, tax credits and other statutory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not exclude Spanish-source income merely because shareholders or customers are non-resident. Allocate income and expenses to the Spanish entity using accounting records and arm's-length principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax losses from prior periods used in the current period, subject to applicable percentage limitations and the statutory minimum offset allowance. Large taxpayers may face stricter percentage limitations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses must belong to the Spanish taxpayer and be supported by filed returns, accounting records and acquisition documentation. Changes in ownership of loss-making companies may restrict use of carried-forward losses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable base after statutory adjustments and loss utilization, applicable tax rate, gross corporate income tax, tax credits, double-tax relief and final tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the ordinary 25% rate unless a documented statutory incentive applies. Treaty relief generally does not reduce Spanish corporate income tax of a Spanish resident company; it principally affects foreign-source taxation and withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payments on account under Modelo 202, Spanish withholding tax credits, prepayments, refunds and balance payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile all Modelo 202 payments and Spanish withholdings to accounting ledgers and bank evidence. Foreign taxes may require separate foreign-tax-credit analysis and documentary support.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of related-party transactions, ownership relationships, intra-group financing, royalties, services, purchases, sales, restructurings and other reportable transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include transactions with non-resident parent companies, affiliates, directors, common-control entities and permanent establishments. Maintain contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation in Spanish or an accepted official-language format.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Tax credits, deductions and supporting schedules
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: R&D and technological innovation credits, double-tax deductions, employment incentives, investment deductions, donations and other applicable deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only credits supported by technical reports, invoices, payroll records, project documentation and statutory eligibility evidence. Foreign grants and subsidies may affect the qualifying expenditure base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Electronic signature and payment or refund
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Electronic submission, payment reference, direct debit where available, bank payment, deferred payment request or refund account.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use an authorized Spanish tax representative where the company lacks the required electronic certificate or Spanish administrative access. Maintain the submitted return, validation code and payment evidence.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing with tax payable generally attracts a voluntary filing surcharge of 1% plus 1% for each additional complete month of delay during the first 12 months. After 12 months, the surcharge is generally 15% plus statutory late-payment interest from the twelfth month. If the tax authority initiates proceedings, formal tax penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax depending on concealment, repeated conduct and aggravating circumstances. Incorrect or incomplete returns may trigger penalties, interest and assessment of omitted tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 202, corporate income tax payments on account, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly payment periods, generally in April, October and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the first 20 calendar days of April, October and December. The large-company calculation method may be mandatory where the statutory turnover threshold is exceeded, and the installment is then based on the current-period tax base rather than only the prior year's final liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax identification number, legal name, tax period and installment number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the Spanish SL's own tax identification number. A foreign parent is not substituted as the taxpayer unless it is itself filing under a Spanish consolidated or permanent-establishment regime.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year corporate tax liability, or current-period tax-base calculation for taxpayers required to use the alternative method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the calculation to Modelo 200, interim accounting data, tax adjustments and group transactions. Do not deduct unverified foreign tax credits or treaty claims.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable percentage, gross installment, credits, prior payments and net amount payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Retain bank confirmation and payment reference. A cash-flow forecast should account for installment payments even where annual taxable income is expected to decline.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late payment may generate the statutory voluntary payment surcharge and late-payment interest. Failure to make an installment can also produce an underpayment in Modelo 200, with interest and tax penalties where the final liability is not correctly settled.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, Informative declaration of related-party transactions and transactions with tax havens, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally filed during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a 31 December year-end, the normal deadline is 30 November of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Counterparty tax identification, country, relationship category, transaction type and valuation method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify foreign counterparties accurately, including parent companies, affiliates, common-control entities and related financing or royalty counterparties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transaction amounts by counterparty and category, including financing, services, goods, royalties, leases, restructurings and transfers of assets or rights.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use consistent accounting and transfer-pricing values. Reconcile declared amounts to invoices, general ledger accounts, customs data and intercompany agreements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Low-tax jurisdiction and special transaction reporting
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions involving jurisdictions listed under applicable Spanish non-cooperative jurisdiction rules and certain special transactions, including restructurings or transfers of business assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Review the current Spanish list and applicable classification at the filing date. Do not rely solely on the counterparty's place of incorporation; assess beneficial ownership and payment routing.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or incorrect filing may trigger formal information-return penalties and, where the omitted information affects taxable income, additional assessment, interest and tax penalties. Transfer-pricing documentation failures may attract transaction-based statutory penalties.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 216, withholding and payment on account for income obtained by non-residents without a permanent establishment, and Modelo 296, annual summary of non-resident withholdings, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic office.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Modelo 216 is generally quarterly, or monthly for large taxpayers; Modelo 296 is annual.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 216 is generally filed within the first 20 calendar days following each quarter, or each month for monthly filers. Modelo 296 is generally filed in January for the preceding calendar year, subject to the official calendar.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident recipient, residence country, tax identification, beneficial-owner information where relevant and income category.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain a valid certificate of tax residence before applying treaty or EU exemptions. Record the direct recipient and beneficial owner where anti-abuse rules require look-through analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Income type, gross amount and withholding
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Dividends, interest, royalties, services or other Spanish-source income, gross payment, applicable rate, relief and tax withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply domestic withholding unless a documented exemption or treaty limitation is available at payment. Maintain contracts, invoices, residence certificates and beneficial-ownership evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate recipient-level information and reconciliation with quarterly or monthly Modelo 216 filings.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile to bank payment files, dividend minutes, loan schedules, royalty ledgers and accounting withholding accounts.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or remit may make the Spanish payer liable for the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest and tax penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% depending on the conduct. Incorrect information returns may incur separate formal penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% domestic withholding on dividends and other profit distributions paid by a Spanish resident company to a non-resident, subject to exemptions and treaty relief. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption may apply to a qualifying EU or EEA corporate parent where minimum ownership, holding-period, subject-to-tax, legal-form and anti-abuse requirements are met. Spanish domestic participation-exemption and anti-abuse rules must be reviewed independently.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a valid certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's competent authority and verify treaty eligibility, beneficial ownership, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose-test considerations, minimum ownership and holding periods, and any domestic anti-abuse provisions. Apply the reduced rate at source only where the payer has sufficient evidence. Otherwise withhold at the domestic rate and allow the recipient to seek a refund through the applicable AEAT procedure, generally Modelo 210. Maintain the certificate, ownership chart, corporate documents, payment records and treaty analysis. Tax-residence certificates should be current under the relevant administrative practice and treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic withholding is generally 19% on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to statutory exemptions, treaty limitations and EU Directive relief. Interest and royalty payments to qualifying associated companies resident in another EU Member State may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, subject to minimum ownership, beneficial ownership, holding-period, legal-form and subject-to-tax conditions. Applicable tax treaties commonly reduce rates, frequently to approximately 5% to 15%, but the precise rate depends on the treaty, income classification and recipient status. Payments to non-cooperative jurisdictions require enhanced review and may be denied relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: For transactions with the same related person or entity, contemporaneous documentation is generally required where the aggregate market value for the tax period exceeds EUR 250,000 for transactions of the same type and under the same valuation method, subject to statutory exemptions and simplified documentation for qualifying small entities. A Master File may be required where the Spanish entity forms part of a qualifying multinational group. Modelo 232 reporting can be triggered by additional thresholds, including aggregate related-party transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 or specific categories exceeding EUR 100,000, depending on the transaction type and applicable rules.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate standalone regime titled Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to certain offshore jurisdictions. Substance is nevertheless material under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule, conflict-in-application doctrine, beneficial-ownership principles, EU anti-abuse rules, interest and royalty exemptions, participation exemptions, controlled foreign company rules, treaty principal-purpose-test standards and anti-conduit analysis. A Spanish SL should maintain real management, personnel or outsourced operational capacity, premises or credible operational infrastructure, commercial risk, decision-making records, bank activity, inventory and customer or supplier functions consistent with its industrial-computing business. A pure conduit, nominee director structure, circular financing or unsupported royalty arrangement creates significant reassessment risk.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and concealed taxable income
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting sales, diverting export proceeds, maintaining parallel accounts, fabricating expenses, concealing related-party payments or claiming unsupported deductions and credits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative tax penalties generally range from 50% to 150% of the unpaid tax, in addition to the tax and interest. Tax fraud may become criminal where the amount defrauded exceeds EUR 120,000 in a tax period, generally carrying imprisonment of 1 to 5 years and a fine of one to six times the amount defrauded. Aggravated cases, including amounts exceeding EUR 600,000 or use of organizations or intermediaries, may carry imprisonment of 2 to 6 years and a fine of two to six times the amount defrauded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers may incur subsidiary or joint and several liability under the Spanish General Tax Law for unpaid taxes, penalties and payment obligations where they caused, tolerated or failed to prevent the breach. Criminal conviction may result in imprisonment, disqualification, asset seizure and civil restitution. A travel ban is not an automatic tax sanction but may be ordered by a criminal or insolvency court where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: False accounting and fraudulent corporate records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Recording fictitious invoices, manipulating inventory or revenue, backdating intercompany agreements, falsifying financial statements or destroying records relevant to tax assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Potential criminal liability for accounting or corporate-document offences, tax reassessment, interest, administrative penalties, director disqualification and civil damages. Sanctions depend on the offence, materiality, intent and resulting harm.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, finance officers and persons who ordered or knowingly approved falsification may face personal criminal prosecution, imprisonment or fines, civil restitution and director disqualification. The corporate form does not protect deliberate personal criminal conduct.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer-pricing manipulation and undocumented related-party dealings
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length prices to foreign affiliates, shifting Spanish profits through unsupported royalties or management fees, using interest-free or inadequately documented loans, or failing to maintain required Local File, Master File or supporting evidence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority may substitute arm's-length values, increase the Spanish taxable base, deny deductions, impose late-payment interest and apply documentation-related penalties. Transaction-based penalties may apply where an adjustment is made or required information is missing or inaccurate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face tax-liability derivation, civil claims and, where concealment is intentional and material, criminal tax exposure. Approval of a commercially unsupported structure is a significant evidentiary factor.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Improper withholding-tax relief and treaty abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Applying a treaty rate without a valid residence certificate, paying dividends, interest or royalties to a conduit entity, misrepresenting beneficial ownership, or relying on EU exemptions without satisfying ownership, subject-to-tax or anti-abuse conditions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Spanish payer may be assessed for the unpaid withholding, interest and penalties generally ranging from 50% to 150% of the unpaid amount. The recipient may lose treaty or directive benefits and face refund denial.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and authorized signatories may incur subsidiary liability where they knowingly approved unsupported relief or failed to implement required controls. Criminal exposure may arise if the arrangement forms part of deliberate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: VAT carousel, customs and export fraud
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using missing-trader structures, false intra-EU supplies, fabricated export evidence, incorrect customs values, circular invoicing or claiming input VAT on non-existent industrial-computer purchases.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: VAT assessment, denial of input credit or zero-rating, interest, administrative penalties and possible criminal tax-fraud prosecution. Customs breaches may also result in duty recovery, penalties, seizure and loss of customs simplifications.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and controlling persons may be personally liable under tax and criminal law where they participated in or knowingly facilitated the fraud. Assets may be frozen or seized; criminal courts may impose imprisonment, fines and civil restitution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting unexplained third-party payments, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner, failing to conduct required customer or supplier due diligence, structuring payments to avoid controls, or ignoring suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Spanish AML legislation, serious and very serious breaches may result in public or private reprimands, monetary fines that can reach statutory maximums of up to EUR 1.5 million or 5% of net worth for the most serious categories, temporary authorization or management restrictions where applicable, and responsible-officer sanctions. Exact limits depend on the breach and applicable statutory category.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers and compliance officers may be sanctioned personally, disqualified or exposed to criminal money-laundering liability where they knowingly participate in concealment or conversion of criminal proceeds. Corporate liability does not eliminate individual liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Profit distribution, insolvency and creditor prejudice
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends while the company lacks distributable profits or reserves, extracting assets before insolvency, repaying insiders preferentially, or transferring valuable technology or inventory to related parties at undervalue.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Unlawful distributions may require restitution with interest and may produce director liability for the company deficit. Insolvency-law consequences can include clawback of transactions, liability for the insolvency estate, disqualification and loss of rights as creditors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be ordered to cover all or part of the insolvency deficit, repay assets, compensate creditors and bear disqualification consequences. Fraudulent asset removal may additionally constitute a criminal offence carrying imprisonment and fines.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to maintain accounting, tax and electronic records
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to keep Spanish accounting books, invoices, inventory records, customs evidence, payroll data, intercompany agreements, tax certificates or electronic filing credentials for the statutory retention period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Formal accounting, invoicing and tax-information penalties may apply, together with estimation of the tax base, denial of deductions, late filing surcharges and interest. Electronic filing failures do not generally excuse statutory deadlines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil and tax liability for failure to organize legally compliant accounting and filing systems. Persistent intentional destruction or concealment of records may create criminal exposure.
